item.content:encoded:
As for the whole fictional character bit, well, we do have an SCP that is the angel guarding what appears to be the Garden of Eden….

And though yes, this is totally a work of fiction and whatnot, it's still interesting to me to link 076 and 073 to the Bible. Given the original story of Cain and Abel, there are all kinds of wonderful interpretations you can make. It could be that the story within the Bible got totally flipped about and twisted around, true. But the interpretation I rather prefer is that Cain got his punishment, and became a rather remorseful, polite fellow indeed over his time on the earth. Abel, originally a far kinder fellow, made a deal with something… else… to survive, and in doing so has become the monstrous fighting machine we all know now.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
…

There are so many things wrong with this post it isn't even funny.

The main thing being that for the majority of Christians, Genesis 1-15 (that would be including Cain and Abel) is completely fictional anyway. It's a myth, written as a counter to other common myths of the day, most specifically the Enuma Elish and the Epic of Gilgamesh. What's important is the meaning, not the contents of the story itself, because it's not meant to be taken as historical fact. Cain and Able's articles hinge on the idea of "what if it was historical fact and got it wrong" which is fine and good, but please remember:

THIS IS FICTION. IT IS A FICTIONAL SHORT STORY ON THE INTERNET, MEANT FOR ENTERTAINMENT, NOT FOR THE IMPARTING OF MORAL LESSONS. IT IS NOT A RELIABLE REPLACEMENT FOR THEOLOGICAL, PHILOSOPHICAL, LITERARY OR HISTORICAL STUDY OF FICTIONAL STORIES MEANT TO IMPART MORAL LESSONS OR HISTORICAL ACCOUNTS OF THE SAME PURPOSE.

e: okay, Imma gonna just walk away from this fer now. Best for everyone involved.

item.content:encoded:
I think the reason people are going to give you a hard time for posts like this isn't that we don't like monsters— that's kind of a thing we all enjoy, here — and more the Draco in Leather Pants tone you're taking.

Constructive comments on SCPs acknowledge the fourth wall. We all gush over writing quality, now and again, but addressing a post as if a character is real is going to attract some sniping. I mean, someone constructed Able, here, so if you're going to praise something, consider what it is the author did— story or style-wise — to affect your emotions so strongly. Thoughtful remarks like that will get you more respect.

Well, it's more out of contempt, or boredom, or insanity. Eternity does funny things to a person's head. I didn't say he was the perfect warrior, it's just that was a factor that helped inspire his creation.

But as you said, it is an entirely subjective category. I mean, they are imprisoning him against his will, most likely have performed numerous experiments on him, some probably lethally invasive, and is pretty much denied an existence he would appreciate.

On the flipside, maybe he's a real monster. A sociopath with a insecurity complex so large, he's got to prove himself to the world, time and again.

Maybe he's insane with boredom, of a death that will not come, so he's driven to do what most people do in games with a similar concept and too much free time.

He could be more animal than man, a vicious attack dog that has forgotten the hand of its master, unable to be used for anything else but bloody deeds.

Maybe he's just a dick. -shrugs-

He is whatever you want to view him as.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This, combined with the main article, absolutely fascinates me. If I could have one SCP on this site exist in real life, as far as I've read, I would choose Able. That may seem strange, but the reason is that I wish I could talk to him - with safety measures in place, of course. I'd like to understand him better. I mean, the article says at one point that he's "a perfect sociopath", but the impression I get is that he's not so much a perfect sociopath as he is a perfect warrior. He's not a monster, because he doesn't particularly enjoy torturing his "victims" - he just kills without any inhibitions, with no empathy for his enemies, which is ideal in a soldier. He also seems to have a strong sense of a warrior's honor - his respect for the unnamed agent, and his comments about said agent deserving to die in direct combat, suggested to me that 1) he believes the best, most honorable way to die is in battle, and 2) he honors a worthy opponent. I'd like to be able to talk to him…no pun intended.
There's just one thing I'm confused about: I thought that Cain was the bad guy, and Abel was the victim? Still, this is one of my favorite SCP's. +1!
